Holding, you buy it and rent it for the money income. You don't care what the house value is, you just rely on the mouthy income. (Dividend)

I tried to host at home first (Deutsche Telekom), got a bad pool rating and moved to Netcup.  Didn't help much. I was thinking about moving again, but without clear understanding what things like 'Client Success Rate' actually represents, its hard to select a new provider.

Regarding peering, the 'Peering Wars' are pretty bad here in the EU. At Netcup, I see some Bufferbloat and TCP Retransmits when the client has some lesser known ISPs like Altibox (Norway) or Play (Poland). Most of the time these are routed via Arelion and it just bottlenecks there. Server admin options to deal with this are limited.

Client Success Rate is the client reported ability to successfully download each file chunk expressed as a percentage.  Failures most often represent a slow client connection or a large network latency between the client and the server.  I think these are rarely VPS issues.  This rate is not within your control for the most part, once you have established a solid network connection, which a VPS typically provides.
